title: Same look, different behaviour
idea: TOOL: two sub-plans can produce the same screen output yet behave differently when stored.

options: No - b returns, it does not print
exercises.explanation: b(5) returns 10 but shows nothing. a prints to the screen; b hands the value back silently.

exercises.prompt: Same a and b. What does 'x = a(5)' store? (a prints n*2)
exercises.explanation: a prints 10 but returns nothing, so x = None. The screen showed 10, but that is not what was stored.

exercises.prompt: Same a and b. What does 'x = b(5)' store? (b returns n*2)
exercises.explanation: b returns 10, so x = 10. Returning is what makes the value available to store.

exercises.prompt: Two sub-plans can look identical on screen yet store different things.
exercises.explanation: Yes. a prints and b returns. Both can show 10, but only b gives you a 10 you can store and reuse.

exercises.prompt: To both SEE the value and STORE it, which sub-plan plus caller works?
options: b (returns), then print(b(5)) in the caller
exercises.explanation: b returns 10, and print(b(5)) shows it AND you can also store b(5). Returning keeps both options.

exercises.prompt: Using b that returns n*2, order the caller code to store AND show the result.
exercises.explanation: Store the returned value first, then print it. Because b returns, x holds 10 and print shows it.

exercises.prompt:
def a(n):
    print(n)

result = a(7) + 1

What goes wrong?
options: a returns None, so None + 1 is an error
exercises.explanation: a only prints, so a(7) is None. You cannot add 1 to None - that is an error. a needed a return.

exercises.prompt: Fix the previous bug. Change a so 'result = a(7) + 1' makes result 8.
options: Make a return n instead of printing it
exercises.explanation: With 'return n', a(7) is 7 and 7 + 1 = 8. A returning sub-plan can join arithmetic; a printing one cannot.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: 'None + 1' failing is a reminder that...
options: a print-only sub-plan hands back None, not the shown value
exercises.explanation: None is what you get with no return. It cannot do math, which is why mixing print and reuse fails.

exercises.prompt: The screen output alone cannot tell you whether a value was returned or just printed.
exercises.explanation: Right. You must look at the code - a return line, not the screen, decides what the caller receives.
